dedupe_keys.name: visitor capacity of three nanjing parks under social distancing agent based simulation yue and co authors ijerph 2021

description: This case study estimates how many visitors three Nanjing parks can hold when people keep social distance, using an agent-based model of visitor movement. Zhi Yue, Jon Bryan Burley, Zhouxiao Cui, Houping Lei and Jing Zhou of Nanjing Forestry University and Michigan State University published it in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health in June 2021. The NetLogo model draws on entrance counts made by park management and checked by the team in 2019 and 2020 at Bailuzhou Park, Xuanwu Lake Park and the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, and on surveyed stay times and visitor types, with rules for targets, path choice by A-star search and crowd avoidance. It finds congestion in every park without control, safe space of 85 to 3,972 square metres per person, and that information for visitors beats layout changes and mandatory rules. Coverage is three parks. Format and access: an open access article. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: the model code is not released and rules are simplified. It informs capacity planning and operation of parks as public green infrastructure during epidemics. Related catalogue records are the US public parks nature-based flood study and the Boston park and street tree inventory.
